title: AgentRunRecord
description: Rich per-transaction telemetry captured by the demo buyer/seller agents (packages/agents) — a different object from Receipt (receipt.schema.json), which is verify_receipt's minimal signed on-chain attestation. This is unpublished research data about Touchstone's own testbed agents: it feeds nobody's print, is never cited as market evidence (docs/methodology.md §2's hierarchy of evidence excludes it explicitly), and exists only so workflow-level questions (retries, latency, routing) can be answered about runs that already happened, since this data cannot be collected retroactively. Every field below is either populated with a real, honestly-derived value or explicitly null — a null always carries a 'why' in its own description, distinguishing 'considered and unavailable' from 'forgotten.'

decimalString.description: A decimal number encoded as a string. Never a JSON number — no floats in money maths.

schema_version.description: Build 1 emits "1.0". Same forward-compatibility convention as Receipt/touchstone-quote: a same-major bump is additive and safe for an existing reader to accept.

run_id.description: Generated at capture time. Not the same value as any RunRecord.run_id (packages/basket measurement runs) — this is a demo-agent transaction, never a basket-measurement execution.

role.description: One real settled transaction produces two records, one per vantage point — a buyer and a seller see genuinely different things (the buyer knows which of two quotes it chose and whether verify_receipt matched; the seller knows the model, provider and execution telemetry). Neither role's record is a subset of the other's.

quote_hash.description: Links this record to the same on-chain settlement Receipt.quote_hash refers to (docs/settlement-metadata.md) — the join key between rich (unpublished) telemetry and the minimal (published-shape) signed attestation.

methodology_version.description: Illustrative in this environment (see packages/agents/src/seller.ts's ILLUSTRATIVE_INDEX_VERSION) until a real print exists to quote against — never presented as a real published methodology version.

model.description: Registry model id. Null only for a buyer record predating this field's population from the chosen quote's own `model` field — should not be null in practice, since the quote always carries it.

provider.description: Null-by-design on a buyer record: a buyer sees the seller's quote and result, never the seller's own registry entry, so it has no provider field to report. Populated directly on a seller record from its own ModelRegistryEntry.

routing_decision.description: Seller-only: whether this call was pinned to registryEntry.host or allowed to route unpinned (SellerOptions.allowUnpinnedRouting). Null-by-design on a buyer record — routing is an internal seller decision a buyer never observes.

usage.description: Null-by-design only if the transaction failed before a result existed. Real token counts on both roles once the seller's 200 response is reached (buyer reads them off the same response body the seller computed).

latency_ms.description: Real adapter call latency, reported by the seller and echoed back to the buyer in the fulfillment response so both roles can record the same true figure.

retry_count.description: Seller-only, via withBackoff's existing onRetry hook (packages/harness/src/retry.ts) — a real, not invented, count of retried attempts before success. Null-by-design on a buyer record: a buyer never sees a seller's internal retry behaviour, only the eventual result.

fallback_count.description: Null-by-design on both roles today: no fallback mechanism exists anywhere in this demo path (a buyer picks between exactly two known sellers by cheapest quote; neither agent retries against a different seller on failure). Recorded as an explicit null, not omitted, so a future reader knows this was considered and found not-yet-applicable, rather than forgotten.

tool_calls.description: Null-by-design on both roles: the demo task is a single-turn completion with no tool-calling in the harness/adapter model at all (build1-spec.md §3's execution settings state 'no tools' explicitly). Recorded as null, not omitted, because the field was considered.

tool_failures.description: Null-by-design on both roles, for the same reason as tool_calls — no tool-calling mechanism exists in the demo path to fail.

quality_gate_result.description: Null-by-design on both roles: a live demo transaction never runs a basket grader (packages/basket) — only a scheduled print's own harness run does that (RunRecord.gate_passed). This field exists so a future workflow-measurement product can populate it once a grading step is added to the demo path, not because one exists today.

human_review_required.description: Null-by-design on both roles: no human-review step exists anywhere in the demo path today. Recorded as null, not omitted, for the same reason as quality_gate_result.

quoted_siu.description: The chosen quote's own `siu` field — available to both roles directly.

actual_siu.description: usdc_paid converted back to SIU via the same quote's rate_usd_per_siu (decimal-string division, never a float) — computable by both roles from data each already has.

usdc_paid.description: The real settled USD amount (TouchstoneEscrow.settle's actualAmount, restated in dollars) — available to both roles.

task_spec_hash.description: keccak256 of the fixed canned task the seller ran (its prompt and output-token ceiling). Null-by-design on a buyer record — a buyer never sees the seller's literal prompt text, only the result, so it has nothing to hash. Populated on every seller record.

receipt_hash.description: keccak256 of this record's own other fields (JCS-canonicalised, this field itself excluded — a hash cannot cover itself, same convention as quote_hash). Not a substitute for Receipt's own signature; this record is unsigned, unpublished telemetry.

verify_receipt_matched.description: Buyer-only: the `matched` value verify_receipt returned for this transaction. Null-by-design on a seller record — a seller never calls verify_receipt itself in this demo.

chosen_seller_label.description: Buyer-only: which of the two known sellers this transaction settled with. Null-by-design on a seller record — a seller has no notion of having been 'chosen' over an alternative it never saw.
